newsitem.title: UK: NatGrid faces 46.3 million pension bill.
newsitem.headline: NatGrid faces 46.3 million pension bill.

text.p: Britain's National Grid Group said on Friday that the pensions ombudsman had ordered it to pay 46.3 million pounds ($75.94 million) including interest to its pension scheme after it lost a ruling.
National Grid said the pension ombudsman had also directed the company to increase its contributions by 600,000 pounds a year. It said it may appeal against the ruling.

The pensions ombudsman ruled that the company should contribute to the company's pension scheme the amounts payable under two of its provisions which were not paid while the scheme was in surplus plus interest.
The surplus was reported in 1992 and National Grid said the valuation was done "in accordance with the rules of the pensions scheme".
"The ombudsman has further directed that the company should now make proper arrangements to deal with the surplus in the scheme," National Grid said in a statement.
The company said it would treat these sums of money as contingent liabilities at the end of the financial year.
